title: Preemptible node transition check‑in — week of 2026-05-12
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes from the infra weekly focused on preemptible/backfill node transition experiments and short-term regional capacity planning. This is rough — action items and open questions at the bottom.

High-level summary:
- Running phased rollout of the preemptible (spot-like) backfill scheduling policy across three regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-northeast1).
- Goal: reclaim 8–12% effective on-demand capacity by safely packing low-priority, latency-insensitive inference jobs during idle windows.
- Current experiment window: 2026-05-05 -> 2026-05-19. Live on 20% of user traffic for each region (canary lanes).

Key metrics (baseline vs week-of-run):
- Average preemption rate (observed): us-west1 5.8%, eu-west1 3.2%, ap-northeast1 7.1%. (higher in apac due to shorter idle tails)
- Mean queue wait for backfill class: 220ms -> 340ms (increase attributable to batching heuristics change).
- P95 token latency for high-priority routes: unchanged (stable at 145ms).
- Utilization bump on spare nodes: +9% across canary nodes, +6% fleet-wide where scheduling policy applied.
- Cost estimate delta (projected monthly): ~‑4.4% net spend if preemptible backfill fully enabled with current settings.

Region notes:
- us-west1:
  - Observed good preemption profile; most preemptions happen between 02:00–04:00 PT when spot reclaim events cluster (correlates with cloud provider maintenance).
  - Need to increase graceful eviction window to 12s (from 6s) for models with KV cache flush jobs (tertiary impact on latency otherwise).

- eu-west1:
  - Lower preemption rates but more variance in short bursts. Suggest trial of 1.1x aggressive packing multiplier to test less conservative consolidation.
  - Ops: handled a transient scheduling loop midday Wednesday (root cause: controller race — SCHED-993). Patch queued.

- ap-northeast1:
  - Highest preemption and slightly higher failure-to-retry percentage for retryable RPCs. Root cause likely shorter spot reclaim TTL + network QoS differences.
  - Immediate mitigation: enable local retry buffer for 500ms on edge router for backfill class only.

Scheduling and runtime adjustments attempted this week:
- Batching heuristic tweak: prefer smaller batches early in response windows for backfill jobs to avoid holding high-priority queueing. This reduced head-of-line blocking but increased average batch count by +12%.
- Introduced soft-priority floor: if high-priority pending tokens > threshold, preemptible placement holds for up to 50ms rather than immediately filling node. Results: fewer evictions of high-priority jobs observed in canary.
- KV-cache warmup probe disabled temporarily to avoid long initial stalls on preemptible nodes; need to re-evaluate impact on cold-start token cost.

Operational incidents this week:
- Wed 2026-05-13 11:23 UTC: scheduling controller retry loop in eu-west1 affecting ~4% of backfill placements for 45m (SCHED-993). Impact limited to backfill class; high-priority remained unaffected. Root cause: edge case in admission controller combined with GC cycle. Hotfix merged, rollout started 2026-05-14.
- Thu 2026-05-14 03:12 PT: higher-than-expected preemption wave in us-west1 causing ~1800 in-flight backfill jobs to be rescheduled. Retry backlog cleared within 6m due to exponential backoff cap tuning. No customer-facing errors.

Validation checks / telemetry to add next week:
- Add delta-tracing for token-level cost per model between preemptible and on-demand serving to quantify quality vs cost tradeoffs more directly.
- Broken-out dashboard: preemption delta by model family (large models tend to see more sensitive KV cache penalties).
- SLA smoke test nightly for each region running 1000 synthetic high-priority requests to catch regressions before canary expansion.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: finalize eviction grace change to 12s and push to canary by 2026-05-16. (blocked by regression test flake)
- Marisol: deploy eu-west1 packing multiplier experiment (+1.1x) and monitor preemption rate over 72h (start 2026-05-15).
- Jun: enable 500ms local retry buffer for backfill on ap-northeast1 and confirm reduction in failure-to-retry metric (done 2026-05-14, validate).
- Olivia: add model-family preemption dashboard tiles and link to model catalog metadata (requested Confluence update).
- Infra SRE: run canary-wide nightly SLA smoke test pipeline and report pass/fail to #infra-canary-health.

Open questions / risks:
- Quality regression risk: some models with large KV caches show higher token-level cost after preemption and cold restarts. Is the 12s grace enough? If not, we may need warm-up-only backfill nodes for certain model families.
- Backfill vs Dedicated capacity: where do we draw the line? Teams are asking for deterministic latency on certain routes that are currently eligible for backfill. Need policy guidance from product on route classification.
- Long tail preemption clustering (provider-level correlated events) could produce correlated retries across regions if timing aligns. Consider randomized backoff seeding or cross-region fallback for critical requests.

Notes to self / meeting shorthand:
- follow-up with Sched team on flaky admission test case (cc: @jun, @kai).
- remind product to publish route-priority matrix by EOD Friday — this determines next canary expansion eligibility.
- file short blameless incident note for Wed scheduling loop once hotfix fully rolls out.

Meeting attendees (quick):
Ethan Cole, Marisol Vega, Jun Park, Olivia Reinhardt, Kai Huang (scheduling), Ramesh Patel (SRE), Ilya Smirnov (runtime)

Conclusion / recommendation:
- Proceed to expand canary to 40% for us-west1 and eu-west1 after current patches land and nightly SLA smoke test passes for 48h. Hold ap-northeast1 at 20% until we confirm retry buffer effect and preemption smoothing.

-- end of notes --
